title: Samsung Galaxy Watch Ultra 2 and Watch 9 Pack Major Health Upgrades
excerpt: Samsung's latest smartwatches bring Heart Health Score, hearing protection alerts, and FDA-cleared sleep apnea detection, powered by a new Snapdragon chip and bigger batteries.
body:
• Samsung launched Galaxy Watch Ultra 2 ($699) and Galaxy Watch 9 ($379+) at Galaxy Unpacked on July 22, with general availability starting August 7.
  • Both watches feature Heart Health Score, Daily Cardio Load tracking, Fitness Index, hearing health monitoring, and FDA-cleared Sleep Apnea detection.
  • The Ultra 2 adds Trail Run mode, real-time hydration guidance, and EN13319-certified diving support down to 40 meters.
  • A new Qualcomm Snapdragon Wear Elite 3nm chip powers both models, with the Ultra 2 packing an 800mAh battery and 5,000-nit display.

Samsung has rolled out its most health-focused smartwatch lineup yet. The Galaxy Watch Ultra 2 and Galaxy Watch 9, unveiled at Galaxy Unpacked on July 22, 2026, center their upgrades around AI-powered biometric monitoring, bigger batteries, and a new processor built for sustained health tracking.

What the New Watches Offer

Both models run on Qualcomm's 3nm Snapdragon Wear Elite chipset — a first for Samsung, which previously used its own Exynos processors. The switch brings improved power efficiency across all-day health monitoring.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=wMx6qJNO0Hc

The shared health suite includes a Heart Health Score that synthesizes heart rate data into an actionable metric, a Daily Cardio Load feature that advises on workout intensity and recovery windows, and a Fitness Index covering strength, body composition, cardio, flexibility, and endurance. A Vitals feature combines five overnight metrics — heart rate, heart rate variability, respiratory rate, skin temperature, and blood oxygen — to establish a personal health baseline.

Both watches also feature a hearing health mode that monitors environmental noise levels and alerts users to potentially damaging sustained exposure, plus an FDA-cleared Sleep Apnea detection feature, pending regulatory approval in specific markets.

Ultra 2: Built for Extremes

The Galaxy Watch Ultra 2, priced at $699, targets outdoor athletes and divers. Its titanium case is 12% thinner than the original Ultra while housing an 800mAh battery — a 35% increase over its predecessor. The 1.52-inch sapphire crystal display peaks at 5,000 nits, making it readable in direct sunlight.

Exclusive Ultra 2 features include Trail Run mode for tracking elevation and terrain impact, a Nutrition Alert system that estimates sweat loss to provide real-time hydration guidance — what Samsung calls the world's first such feature in a smartwatch — and full diving support with IP69K, 10ATM, and EN13319 certifications. A dedicated diving app, co-developed with equipment manufacturer Mares, automatically tracks depth, duration, and water temperature.

Watch 9: Everyday Health Tracking

The Galaxy Watch 9 comes in 40mm ($379 Bluetooth, $429 LTE) and 44mm ($409 Bluetooth, $459 LTE) sizes with an aluminum case. Battery capacities sit at 390mAh and 445mAh respectively, with displays peaking at 3,000 nits. Storage is 32GB compared to the Ultra 2's 64GB.

While it lacks diving and trail-running features, the Watch 9 shares the full health monitoring suite. Both models also gain raise-to-talk functionality with Google Gemini — a feature first introduced on the Pixel Watch 4 — letting users query the AI assistant without pulling out their phone.

What It Means for Wearable Health

Samsung's approach reflects an industry-wide shift from adding new sensors to extracting more intelligence from existing ones, according to Gizmodo. Rather than packing in novel hardware, the company is layering AI-driven interpretation over its BioActive sensor array.

The $30 price increases across the lineup — the Watch 9 starts $30 higher than the Watch 8, while the Ultra 2 is $50 more than the 2024 original — position Samsung's health-tracking wearables directly against Apple's latest Watch offerings. Both watches run Wear OS 7 with Samsung's One UI 9 Watch and require an Android 13+ device with at least 1.5GB of RAM.

Pre-orders opened July 22, with the watches hitting shelves on August 7. The Galaxy Watch Ultra 2 is available in Titanium Silver and Titanium Gray, while the Watch 9 comes in Graphite, Silver, and Cream.
